stories.title: Misiorowski Takes His First Loss — "Gets Tagged for the First Time" by the Mets
stories.angle: The NL Cy Young favorite (-550) with a 1.68 ERA took his first notable loss of the 2026 season Thursday against the Mets. Before today: 13-5, 1.68 ERA, 216 Ks in 145 IP. How one bad start frames the bigger Cy Young conversation — and whether the award is still his.

x_posts.label: Post 1-1
x_posts.text: The Mets tagged Misiorowski for the first time in 2026. He came in 13-5 with a 1.68 ERA and a Cy Young market of -550. One loss doesn't change that — but it changes the narrative. The flawless run is over. #Brewers #MLB

x_posts.label: Post 1-2
x_posts.text: Misiorowski's first loss of the year doesn't mean the Cy Young is open. He's 13-6 with a 1.68 ERA and 216 strikeouts. One bad start in August is not a collapse — it's a data point. The market still has him -550. #Brewers #MLB

article.headline: Misiorowski Gets Tagged for the First Time. The Mets End His Flawless 2026 Run.

stories.title: PCA NL MVP — Cubs Drop Back-to-Back to D-backs, Lead Still Holds
stories.angle: D-backs took back-to-back games from the Cubs (Waldschmidt walk-off Aug 25; 2-0 Aug 26). Cubs now 76-57. PCA (.281 BA, 33 HR, 83 RBI, 32 SB, 7.8 fWAR) still leads the NL MVP poll with 29 of 37 first-place votes — but the Cubs' losing streak adds pressure to the team-success angle in the race.

x_posts.text: PCA: .281 BA, 33 HR, 83 RBI, 32 SB, 7.8 fWAR. Cubs just dropped back-to-back to the D-backs. Ohtani is 8 fWAR back. The Cubs' slide adds a team-performance question to the MVP conversation — but PCA's numbers still lead. #Cubs #MLB

stories.title: Yordan Alvarez Triple Crown Chase — ZiPS Says 66.5% Odds, Cabrera 2012 Was the Last
stories.angle: Alvarez leads the AL in batting average (.329-.330), home runs (35), and RBI (84-85). ZiPS projects 66.5% odds. His batting average lead is "essentially insurmountable" (+29 points). 7-game hitting streak with 4 HRs. The last player to win the Triple Crown was Miguel Cabrera in 2012.

stories.title: Dustin May Survives a 106 MPH Comebacker — Brewers Win 8-1 Anyway
stories.angle: On the first pitch of his Mets start Tuesday, A.J. Ewing lined a comebacker at 106 mph off Dustin May's back. May was removed, diagnosed with a right scapula contusion (bruised shoulder blade) — negative X-rays. Robert Gasser came in and delivered roughly 6 innings of emergency relief as the Brewers dominated anyway. May's status going forward.

x_posts.label: Post 5
x_posts.text: On the first pitch of his start Tuesday, a 106 MPH line drive off A.J. Ewing's bat hit Dustin May in the back. Removed immediately. Diagnosis: right scapula contusion. Negative X-rays. Robert Gasser took over and the Brewers won 8-1. #Brewers #MLB

article.headline: A 106 MPH Line Drive Off His Back on the First Pitch. Then the Brewers Won 8-1 Without Dustin May.
